title: DECIDE-2 Substudy I: Supported Advance Care Decision-Making in Dementia - An Integrated Approach for Practical Implementation
summary:
Dementia is a terminal illness and puts considerable burden on affected individuals and their caregivers. Caregivers serving as proxy decision makers face uncertainty with regard to end-of-life-decisions for people with dementia, who loose their decision-making capacity.
Advance healthcare planning can enable individuals to receive treatment and care in line with their wishes, even if they are unable to provide consent. Current concepts of advance healthcare care planning tend to overlook psychological decision-making processes. Recent research has therefore focused on interventions that provide support for the psychological decision-making process in order to make the benefits of advance healthcare planning accessible to people with dementia. 
In the current study, the evaluated concept of Advance Care Decision-Making (ACD) will be investigated by integrating it into the already implemented concept of Dementia Care Management (DeCM). We assume that the process of supported decision-making is facilitated for people with dementia who participate in ACD, thereby improving their capacity to consent. The study aims to reduce proxy burden and to increase autonomy of people with dementia in making advance care and end-of-life-decisions.
The study will be conducted in cooperation with four partners from the regional Dementia Care Management Network in Siegen-Wittgenstein. N = 150 patients with a confirmed diagnosis of mild to moderate dementia (F00-F03) or mild cognitive impairment (F06.7) will be recruited. Study participants will be assigned to one of two groups and either attend DeCM appointments and two to three ACD appointments or DeCM appointments only. In both groups, we will look at participants' advance care planning documents and the at proxy burden. In addition, we will look at further variables such as participants'  autonomy and patient-caregiver congruence in preferences.
